default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-248.title: Prior-sessions opening-price poke fade
E-248.hypothesis: The opening-auction prices of the last few sessions are where each day's overnight orders were matched, and desks that anchor on them keep resting orders there; a bar that trades through such a price and closes back meets those resting orders, so the small break buyers (sellers) are trapped; fade back from the level.

E-249.title: Multi-session rolling VWAP hold
E-249.hypothesis: The volume-weighted price of the last few sessions plus today is the average cost of the swing holders; when price returns to it from one side and closes back on that side, those holders defend their cost basis (add or cover) instead of the intraday traders who pushed into it; trade away from the level.

E-250.title: Multi-day range quartile poke fade
E-250.hypothesis: Swing traders grid their orders on the quarter, half and three-quarter marks of the last few sessions' range; a bar that pokes through one of those marks and closes back has met that resting size, and the intraday push through it has no follow-through; fade it.

E-251.title: Prior-sessions initial-balance edge fade
E-251.hypothesis: The first-hour high/low of recent sessions is the range that the opening institutions defended on those days, and Market Profile users carry it forward as reference; a later poke through such an old edge that closes back is absorbed by the same responsive traders, so fade it.

E-252.title: Vortex cross fade
E-252.hypothesis: The Vortex indicator cross is a stock retail trend trigger that fires after the short swing already happened; the traders who enter on it supply the liquidity the earlier movers exit into, so the swing reverts; fade the cross.

E-253.title: Prior sessions' peak-volume price hold
E-253.hypothesis: The price of the heaviest-volume bar of each recent session (outside the auctions) is where the largest participant of that day transacted; that participant defends or re-enters there, so a return to the price that closes back on its side is held; trade away from the level.

E-254.title: Daily moving-average poke fade
E-254.hypothesis: The 5/9/20-day moving averages of daily closes are plotted on almost every WIN daily chart, and swing traders rest entries and exits on them; an intraday poke through the daily average that closes back meets that resting size, not an empty book, so fade it.

E-255.title: Prior-session swing-point poke fade
E-255.hypothesis: Yesterday's intraday swing highs and lows are the levels chart traders mark overnight, with stops and fresh orders just around them; a poke through one that closes back means the stops were taken and the resting counter orders won, so the late breakout traders are trapped; fade it.

E-256.title: Prior closing-range break follow
E-256.hypothesis: The high/low of yesterday's last half hour to hour bounds the price where the overnight positions were opened, and those holders' stops sit just beyond it; a close through the closing range forces them out and their exits extend the move, so follow the break.

E-257.title: Prior settlement-close hold
E-257.hypothesis: Each recent session's close is the zero line of variation margin for positions opened that day; holders defend it to avoid paying margin, so a return to such a close that ends the bar back on its side is held; trade away from the level.
